parsed.why: Same-sex conduct is criminalised amid documented police harassment, non-investigation, public hostility, and severe identity-targeted prison violence. Trans-specific harm is documented, though border treatment is unknown and resort areas appear more insulated.

The national law carries extreme prison penalties, with recent arrests and documented police tactics including raids and digital entrapment. Severe public violence against a trans woman and a hostile, state-backed climate make discovery exceptionally dangerous.

Gender-identity protections, lawful gender-marker changes, community infrastructure, and broad traveller acceptance are positive. Uneven enforcement, under-reporting, political disinformation, and occasional disruption or friction remain, without documented severe visitor-facing targeting.

Strong formal protections and self-declaration coexist with recent reports of rising intimidation and assault, including recurring app ambushes; hate-crime recording and enforcement are imperfect. These risks matter, though no universal visitor restriction is documented.

Authorities use morality and cybercrime laws to target LGBT people and activists, with intimidation, online exposure, and coerced closures; public attitudes are hostile. Visitor-specific enforcement is unproven, but these documented practices make outing materially risky.
